RICHFIELD SERIES
The Richfield series consists of deep, nearly level and gently undulating and undulating, well-drained soils on high terraces and hills and ridges that border river valleys. Slopes range from 0 to 8 percent. They formed in silt loam and silty clay loam alluvium transported by water and wind at elevations of 3100 to 3600 feet.
The vegetation is mainly western wheatgrass, prairie junegrass, big sage, plains reedgrass and winterfat. Annual precipitation is 14 to 15 inches, mean annual soil temperature is 47 to 49 degrees F., the frost free season is 110 to 120 days.
Typically, the surface layer is grayish brown silty clay loam about 9 inches thick. The subsoil is brown silty clay loam about 10 inches thick. The substratum is light brownish gray silt loam to 60 or more inches.
Permeability is moderately slow, the effective rooting depth is 60 or more inches. Available water holding capacity is 10 to 11 inches.
These soils are used for dry cropland and range. They are suitable for irrigation.
A typical profile of Richfield silty clay loam, cultivated 356 feet north and 240 feet east of the W 1/4 corner of Sec. 10, T. 2 S., R. 34 E.
Apl 0 to 7 inches, grayish brown (10YR 5/2) silty clay loam, very dark grayish brown (10YR 3/2) moist; weak, very fine granular structure; hard, friable, sticky and slightly plastic; a few fine roots; clear smooth boundary.
Ap2 7 to 9 inches, grayish brown (10YR 5/2) heavy silty clay loam, dark brown (10YR 3/2) moist; weak, coarse blocky strucuture; hard, friable, slightly sticky and plastic; a few very fine roots; abrupt smooth boundary.
9 to 13 inches, brown (10YR 5/3) silty clay loam, dark brown (10YR 4/3) moist; moderate, medium prismatic structure breaking to moderate, medium blocks; hard, friable, sticky and plastic; a few very fine roots; common, very fine pores; patches of thin clay films on ped surfaces; clear wavy boundary.
13 to 19 inches, light yellowish brown (2.5Y 6/3) silty clay loam, olive brown (2.5Y 4/3) moist; weak, medium prismatic structure parting to weak, medium blocks; hard, friable, sticky and plastic; a few very fine roots; many very fine pores; slightly effervescent; a few, fine soft masses of lime; gradual wavy boundary.
